newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia says domestic fuel prices not to rise.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia says domestic fuel prices not to rise.

text.p: The Indonesian government will not raise domestic fuel oil prices this year, the official Antara news agency reported on Sunday.
It quoted Mines and Energy Minister Ida Bagus Sudjana as saying on Saturday: "Domestic fuel oil prices will remain at their present level until at least the end of this year."
He said after inspecting an oil storage facility in north Sumatra that the government had surplus funds from increased crude oil prices on the world market to offset domestic fuel subsidies.
Indonesia is Asia's only member of the Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC).
Sudjana was also quoted as saying the increase in the world price of crude oil had affected the price of producing domestic fuel oils in general.
The cost of importing crude oil for refining in Indonesia now accounted for as much as 70 percent of the country's fuel oil production costs, he said.
Antara said Sudjana denied allegations that the government was holding down the price of domestic fuel oil because 1997 was a general election year.
